standard_prerequisites: Statement hypothesis: L = K(alpha) of degree e with a = alpha^e in K, and every e-th root of unity in L lies in K
Same chapter: multiplicativity of degrees in towers (lemma-multiplicativity-degrees)
core_obligations: Degree observation: for d | e, x^{e/d} - a in K[x] has root alpha^d so [K(alpha^d) : K] <= e/d, while alpha is a root of x^d - alpha^d over K(alpha^d) so [L : K(alpha^d)] <= d; tower multiplicativity forces equality in both
If alpha^d lies in the subextension L' (with d = [L : L']), then K(alpha^d) subset L' and both L/K(alpha^d) and L/L' have degree d, so L' = K(alpha^d)

In general: the minimal polynomial P of alpha over L' divides x^e - a and has degree d; its roots are of the form zeta_i alpha with zeta_i^e = 1, so its constant term is c = (prod zeta_i) alpha^d in L'; zeta = prod zeta_i is an e-th root of unity lying in L, hence in K by hypothesis; so alpha^d = zeta^{-1} c in L', reducing to the previous case
proof_roadmap: Prove the degree observation by the two polynomial bounds and multiplicativity
Handle the case alpha^d in L' by the degree count
Derive alpha^d in L' in general from the constant term of the minimal polynomial
